newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Astra should remain diversified.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Astra should remain diversified.

text.p: Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said on Wednesday that the government would like to see shareholdings in the country's largest automobile manufacturer Astra International remain diversified.
"Astra is better as a public company...(it should) not belong to any one family, or to a certain group," Murdiono told reporters.

Asked whether the Nusamba group, to which President Suharto is linked and which has expressed an interest in acquiring a stake in the company, would take up a majority shareholding, Murdiono said: "I don't think so."
"At the moment in Astra there is no majority (shareholder)," he said.
"Once there is a big shareholder, that person can take control," Murdiono said, adding that would not be a wise move.

Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three cooperatives headed by Suharto. It announced its interest in taking up a stake in Astra after tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna bought 9.81 percent of the automobile company.
Cigarette firm PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, headed by Putera Sampoerna, then said a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake.

The purchases gave Putera Sampoerna effective control over the single-largest holding in the company. PT Sampoerna announced earlier this week that it was ready to sell the stake bought by its subsidiary.
